correctness.rationale: For every d>=2 and aperture in (0,pi/2], both proposed ellipsoid branches satisfy exact cone tangency c²=a²+cot²(theta)b² and maximize the quadratic squared-radius function q(u) at either the tip or the internal latitude. At the specified apex-dependent coordinates, two explicit finite sets of normalized contact points carry strictly positive weights with first moment zero and covariance the identity, proving maximality among all ellipsoids by the affine John criterion. Both branches match at sin²(theta)=1/d, and direct logarithmic differentiation yields the jump -2d. The embedded checker passed exact rational containment identities and independent finite numerical comparisons; proof is analytical and does not infer infinity from the checks.

value.rationale: This natural curved-cap/cone intersection family has two different active supporting-boundary mechanisms. The result classifies exactly the John ellipsoid for all dimensions and aperture angles, gives constructive global John certificates and sharp contact thresholds, and reveals a nonanalytic C1-but-not-C2 volume transition with dimension-specific jump -2d. Those structural features are not routine renaming of the flat-cone or parallel-slab cases and supply an explicit benchmark for ellipsoidal approximation of conical ball intersections.
